title: Conrad Centre city-led operating model
subtitle: Also: advisory committee term extensions, Artist in Residence appointment, and new and repealed corporate policies.
overview: The Finance and Corporate Services Committee's main item was a new operating model for the Conrad Centre for the Performing Arts. The committee recommended that the city lead the venue, with a hybrid staffing approach, and that Green Light Arts provide mentorship to renting groups until June 30, 2026. Rental agreements and fees would be handled by the Director of Culture & Entertainment. The recommendation is subject to final ratification of the 2025 budget {{vote:m4}}. The committee also asked staff to report back a year after the model starts.

The committee recommended a package of corporate policy changes. It includes amended and repealed policies, two policies required under the Municipal Act (Council-staff relations, and pregnancy and parental leave for members of Council), and a new policy template {{vote:m3}}. It also recommended extending the terms of advisory committee and tribunal members until successors are appointed {{vote:m1}}. It recommended appointing the 2024 Artist in Residence {{vote:m2}}.

All of these are recommendations. Council must adopt them before they take effect. For residents, they affect how a city-owned performing arts venue will be run and booked, and how Council's policies are managed.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended a city-led operating model for the Conrad Centre, subject to final ratification of the 2025 budget.
The committee recommended authorizing an agreement with Green Light Arts to provide mentorship services to renting organizations until June 30, 2026.
The committee recommended delegating approval of rental agreements and rental fees to the Director of Culture & Entertainment or designate.
The committee recommended approving the Master Policy edits and new template, and amending or repealing the listed policies.
The committee recommended approving a Pregnancy and Parental Leave Policy for Members of Council and a Council Staff Relations Policy.
The committee recommended extending 2022-2024 appointments to advisory committees and quasi-judicial tribunals until successors are appointed.
The committee recommended appointing Ellie Anglin as the 2024 Artist in Residence and authorizing the Mayor and Clerk to sign an agreement.

debate: Delegates and councillors broadly supported a city-led model for the Conrad Centre. They argued an impartial operator could put the artist community first, and that the venue is complex and needs specialized staff and investment.

One delegate from a local theatre group urged patience and suggested days of use as a key success measure, alongside revenue and audience numbers. The delegate also asked that community stakeholders be involved in hiring the venue's staff.

Staff said key performance indicators would cover equity, utilization, artist participation and attendance. Staff also noted that equipment, seating, staging and lobby visibility need review, and that those needs would come forward during budget time.

One councillor said sustainability should be the goal, noting that Kitchener taxpayers already carry much of the region's arts and culture support. That councillor asked for an update during the mentorship period, and staff agreed. The report-back request was added to the recommendation.

On corporate policies, one councillor asked about administratively approved policies and whether Heritage Kitchener's terms of reference should allow two council members instead of one. Staff said council can appoint more than one member and the terms could be amended if that becomes standard practice.
